mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the decision is interpreted as a pre-emptive hike, which raises expected discount rates and dampens equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in similar pre-hike regimes are not statistically lower than post-hike periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2.5% in a month, it signals accelerating inflation expectations, which compresses near-term discounting and is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, positive 20-day forward returns occur in >70% of similar inflation acceleration events (binomial test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in HOUST (industrial production) and a decline in PAYEMS (labor employment) suggests a structural weakening in domestic demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 5 consecutive such dual-move events, the 20-day forward return is never negative (binomial test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls by more than 0.5 percentage points in a month, it indicates labor market softening and a risk of wage moderation, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In 3 prior similar softening episodes, the 20-day forward return was not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO reading above 104.0 (2017=100) in a month coinciding with a decline in RSAFS (retail sales) suggests a supply-side shock that outpaces demand, predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In 4 analogous events, the 5-day forward return is not statistically worse than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained period where FEDFUNDS remains below 1.00% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to exhibit positive forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to lower real borrowing costs and improved risk appetite.
failure_condition: Across 10 such regimes, the 60-day forward return is not statistically higher than the mean of non-loose regimes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE remains above 6.5% for two consecutive months, it signals tight labor markets that support equity risk premia, predicting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In 5 prior similar episodes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A coincident decline in both HOUST (industrial production) and GDPC1 (personal consumption) by at least 2% in the prior month indicates a dual-demand shock, which tends to produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In 3 prior dual-demand contractions, the 20-day forward return is not negative (binomial test p < 0.05).
